steps.title: Checkpoint manifest schema + contract encoding
steps.description: Freeze CheckpointManifest/1.0 with GENERATION-LEVEL lockstep atomicity (codex r1 MAJOR 2): a checkpoint is one generation directory gen-<absolute_day>-<run_name>/ staged in full before any commit signal — ALL authoritative state files (mind, world, RNG, identity) written into the staging dir, per-file sha256 recorded in the manifest, fsync, then the manifest itself renamed into place LAST as the sole commit boundary. An uncommitted generation is invalid by definition and swept on next start (recovery rule); the newest committed generation is last-known-good and is NEVER auto-deleted (retention rule). This REPLACES the legacy world-checkpoint block in the turn driver (cloud-init/user-data runner section) — the legacy writer is removed, not wrapped. Manifest fields: every convene-contract field plus per-file checksums, generation id, parent generation id+hash, committed marker semantics. COMMIT REPRESENTATION (codex r2 MODERATE): the manifest file at its final path IS the single authoritative commit token — no separate marker file; presence of a checksum-valid manifest at <generation>/manifest.json = committed, anything else = not. COLLISION RULE: a generation id that already exists as a committed generation is a fail-closed refusal (STATUS=checkpoint-collision:<id>) — never overwrite, never auto-suffix; the caller must choose a new run_name.

steps.title: Mind-state + RNG lineage save/load
steps.description: Mind-state + RNG lineage save/load with an EXPLICIT STATE INVENTORY (codex r1 MAJOR 1): the first S1 deliverable is state-inventory.md, produced by a mechanical audit — grep every RNG consumer (Math.random, seeded PRNGs, shuffle/sample helpers) and every mutable module-level state across tools/ant-hive-world/*.js — listing EVERY stream and consumer by file:line: hive network parameters (weights/biases per layer), controller/optimizer accumulators, entropy/exploration state, training counters, event queues and pending effects, per-agent RNG streams (root seed + counter each), the sim RNG, config/architecture hashes. Serialization must cover the complete inventory; the inventory is itself reviewed at S4. Save integrates into the S0 generation writer (one atomic generation = mind + world + RNG + identity). Load restores byte-identical state: save->load->save produces identical checksums; a restored run's first N decisions match a continued run's under identical frozen inputs.

steps.title: Resume path + halt-for-repair in the turn driver
steps.description: Resume path + halt-for-repair with EXACT semantics (codex r1 MAJOR 3): job.env gains one field, RESUME_FROM=<generation-id> where <generation-id> is the guest-local generation dir basename (gen-<absolute_day>-<run_name>; coordinator default, operator-overridable). Validation ORDER, each stage failing closed with STATUS=resume-failed-halt:<stage>:<reason> and nonzero exit and ZERO state mutation: (1) generation dir exists; (2) manifest present with committed marker; (3) schema/code version compatibility; (4) per-file checksum verification; (5) parent-linkage continuity. Only after all five pass does restore begin. BINDING POINT: the resume gate is the FIRST act of run-live.js (the turn driver) after job.env parsing — it executes BEFORE any fresh-mind initialization, world load, or RNG seeding; on any refusal the driver exits with no state object ever constructed. The legacy checkpoint writer replacement (S0) and this gate land in the SAME slice so no code path exists where the old writer and new reader coexist. Absent RESUME_FROM = explicit fresh start, recorded as fresh_start=true in turn provenance. EXACT CALL SITE (codex r3): the gate is a new resolveResumeOrFreshStart(jobEnv) invoked in run-live.js's entry sequence IMMEDIATELY after argument/job.env parsing and BEFORE the existing state-construction block codex located at run-live.js:77-137 — that block becomes reachable only via the gate's return (either a validated restore handle or an explicit fresh-start token). Refusals write STATUS via the same courier STATUS path the runner already uses and exit nonzero from within the gate. cloud-init/user-data change is now DEFINITE, not 'if needed': the runner section forwards RESUME_FROM from job.env into the driver invocation. run-job.ps1 gains -ResumeFrom passthrough writing the field verbatim.

steps.title: Local continuity control (execution verification)
steps.description: Local continuity control, FROZEN-INPUT REPLICATED five-arm design (codex r1 MAJOR 4 + r2 MAJOR 4): identical frozen input packets across all arms; n=2 replicates per arm. Arm A: checkpointed lineage — 150 ticks, checkpoint at gen boundary, resume, 150 more. Arm A-PRIME: uninterrupted continuation — 300 ticks straight through with A's exact seeds and inputs; the EQUIVALENCE STANDARD: A's post-resume trajectory must match A-prime's ticks 151-300 (decision-stream comparison; byte-equality target, any divergence enumerated and explained or the arm fails). Arm B: fresh-seed control (new root seeds). Arm C: shuffled-RNG control — same root seeds, per-stream assignment permuted. Arm D: tamper test — corrupt one file in a COPY of a committed generation, prove refusal at the checksum stage. Pass = A equivalent-to-A-prime (resume is a true continuation) AND A/A-prime replicably divergent from B and C (state, not seeds, carries behavior) AND D refuses. Fresh arms double as regression check against r6/r7 behavior shape. Evidence: state-inventory.md, continuity-evidence.json (per-arm run ids, checksums, decision-stream diffs, divergence metrics), arm-*/ outputs under _dev/state/checkpoint-continuity-test/. FROZEN-INPUT SEMANTICS (codex r3): 'frozen inputs' is defined concretely — (a) TIME-DERIVED SEEDS ARE ELIMINATED as part of S1: every seed currently derived from wall-clock (run-live.js:118-126,186-210 region) is replaced by explicit root seeds carried in job.env/provenance, so no arm's behavior depends on invocation time; (b) any external decision inputs (world-mind-decision.json operator-console packets) are either ABSENT for all S3 arms (default: the control runs use no console packets) or, if a packet is used, it is a byte-identical recorded file replayed to every arm and hashed into continuity-evidence.json; (c) run/episode identity fields feed provenance but MUST NOT feed any RNG or decision path — the S1 inventory explicitly verifies this non-dependence.
